PIT-Wasserstein: A Calibration Metric for Probabilistic Estimators

A dispersion calibration metric for probabilistic estimators, disentangled from bias and sharpness. Originally published as Supplementary Appendix 2 of Challen & Danon (2025), “Instantaneous Reproduction Number Estimation From Modelled Incidence”; this repository is the extension into a standalone paper titled “Diagnosing miscalibration with PIT-Wasserstein metrics”.

The R package documentation has resources on how to use the package and instructions to reproduce the figures from the upcoming paper.

The Lean proof library gives the asymptotic null laws for all three significance tests and instructions for importing them into another Lean project.

Installation

pitw is hosted on the AI4CI r-universe. Installation of releases from there is as follows:

options(repos = c(
  "ai4ci" = 'https://ai4ci.r-universe.dev/',
  CRAN = 'https://cloud.r-project.org'))

# Download and install pitw in R
install.packages("pitw")

You can install the development version of pitw from GitHub with:

# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("ai4ci/pit-wasserstein")

Core concepts

The paper defines three metrics for assessing probabilistic estimators and differentiating between, bias, dispersion miscalibration, and skill-spread decoupling.

Baseline PIT-Wasserstein (\(B_{pit}\))

\[B_{pit} = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n{|u_i - rank_i|}\]

Where \(rank_i = (i-0.5)/n\) and \(u_i\) are the PIT values.

  • Range: [0, 0.5]. Zero = perfect calibration and zero bias.
  • Property: Symmetric on log-calibration for a given bias.
  • Validated: Dependent on bias, dispersion calibration and sharpness in simulation.

Adjusted PIT-Wasserstein (\(U^*_{pit}\))

\[U_{pit} = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n{|u_{i,adj} - rank_i|}\]

Where \(rank_i = (i-0.5)/n\) and \(u_{i,adj}\) are the bias-adjusted PIT values.

  • Range: [0, 0.5]. Zero = perfect calibration.
  • Property: Symmetric on log-calibration — conservative and overconfident estimators of equal magnitude score equally.
  • Validated: Independent of bias and sharpness in simulation.

Directed PIT-Wasserstein (\(D^*_{pit}\))

\[D_{pit} = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n{(rank_i - u_{i,adj}) \times \operatorname{sgn}(0.5-rank_i)}\]

  • Range: [-0.25, +0.25]
  • Direction: Positive = overconfident (U-shaped PIT histogram); Negative = conservative (dome-shaped).

All three metrics have significance tests based on large-sample reference distributions for independent PIT values. The adjusted tests use reference laws derived for the Gaussian location model.

Summary

The adjusted PIT-Wasserstein (\(U^*_{pit}\)) combines:

  1. Bias adjustment before PIT uniformity assessment (no other metric does this)
  2. Wasserstein/L1 distance rather than sup-norm (PCE) or binning (reliability diagrams)
  3. Signed direction (\(D^*_{pit}\)) distinguishing overconfidence from over-conservatism
  4. Validation showing it is independent of bias and sharpness
